title: Pinch-pot cat figurine
subtitle: A sitting cat built from a pinch pot body, with an added head, ears, and tail
excerpt: A sitting cat figurine in air-dry clay uses a rounded pinch pot as the body, with a small ball head, two triangular ear flaps, and a coiled tail attached at leather-hard stage. Finished height is 10-12 cm. No kiln needed.
sourceNotes: Animal figurine construction derived from first principles. Air-dry clay.

glossaryTerms.definition: A vessel formed by pressing the thumb into a ball of clay and pinching the walls outward
Roughening both surfaces and applying diluted clay before pressing them together for a strong join
The stage at which clay holds its shape firmly but is still damp enough to join additional pieces

content.text: A sitting cat built from a
pinch pot

body has stable proportions because the rounded pot form naturally suggests a cat's tucked-in seated posture. The head, ears, and tail are added pieces. The whole figure is decorated and sealed after drying. No kiln needed.

materials.name: Clay slip (same clay thinned with water)

content.text: Making the body
Wedge 200 g of clay into a smooth ball. Pinch it open into a rounded bowl about 10 cm in diameter and 6 cm tall. The walls should be 8 mm thick for stability.
Turn the pinch pot upside down. This is the cat's body , the open side is now the base. Press the base flat on a board to give the cat a stable sitting platform.
Smooth the outside of the dome body with a damp sponge.
Making the head, ears, and tail

Head: roll 60 g of clay into a slightly flattened sphere, about 6 cm across. Score the bottom of the head and the top of the body dome. Apply slip to both. Press together and blend the neck join with a wooden rib.

Ears: pinch two small triangles from thin slabs, 2 cm tall, 2 cm base. Score the underside of each ear and the top of the head where they will sit. Slip and press. Position them slightly apart on the top of the head, angling slightly outward.

Face: use a needle tool to press two small almond-shaped eye indentations on the front of the head. Add a tiny nose triangle below the eyes. Score two fine whisker lines from the nose outward on each side.
Tail: roll a coil 15 cm long, 1 cm diameter, tapering to a point. Curl it into a half-loop. Use
Score-and-slip
the base end of the tail to the base of the body dome, at the back. The tail curls around one side of the body.
Drying, painting, and sealing
Allow the figurine to dry completely at room temperature, loosely covered for the first day. Once
leather-hard

, check all joins and blend any gaps. Paint with acrylic in any colour , a plain grey-white sits well. Add tabby stripes with a fine brush at leather-hard or after drying. Seal with two coats of matte varnish.
Variations
Build a dog by giving the head a longer snout and drooping ears instead of triangular ones.
Make a pair of cats in different sizes as a shelf display.
Add a small hollow to the body before turning it over, and fill with dried herbs or a tiny LED tealight.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Head cracked at the neck join
items.cause: Join made when one or both pieces were too dry for slip to bond
items.fix: Dampen the crack, work fresh slip into it, and press closed. Support the head with a small clay prop while the repair dries

items.cause: Ears were too thin at the base and the join area was not large enough
items.fix: Re-attach with slip and a larger scored contact area. Thicken the ear bases by pressing a small reinforcing coil around the joint
